_notes: German (de-DE) taxonomy. 10 grammar + 10 vocabulary subs, mirroring FR/PT structure so the runtime stays language-agnostic. German-specific decisions: (1) Replaced FR's 'relative_pronouns' sub with a dedicated 'cases_declension' sub — the single biggest German-learner struggle (Nom/Akk/Dat/Gen marking on articles/adjectives/pronouns), with no clean FR/PT parallel. Relative pronouns themselves live as patterns inside 'complex_sentences' since German relative pronouns are basically declined demonstratives plus the case logic, more naturally taught alongside subordinate clauses. (2) 'present_conjugation' explicitly includes separable verbs and modal verbs as core patterns — these dominate beginner production in German and are not cleanly an FR analog. (3) 'past_tenses' centers on Perfekt vs Präteritum (the FR passé-composé vs imparfait analog but with different register triggers — Perfekt is colloquial spoken default; Präteritum is written-narrative and the fixed set sein/haben/modals). (4) 'subjunctive' is Konjunktiv II in everyday use (würde + irrealis); Konjunktiv I appears only as a reported-speech pattern. (5) 'prepositions' is structured around the Akkusativ/Dativ/Genitiv split and the two-way (Wechselpräpositionen) Akk-motion / Dat-location contrast. (6) 'complex_sentences' folds verb-final word order in subordinate clauses and the case-marked relative pronouns. (7) Vocabulary patterns localized: Anmeldung/Krankenkasse/Finanzamt/BAföG replace FR CAF/impôts and PT CPF/INSS; Brötchen/Mittagessen/Bäckerei replace FR plats-typiques; Deutsche Bahn/ICE/Fahrkarte replace FR billets-reservations; Sie-vs-du is the single most important register axis.
